prompt: A town has $1250$ people and its population DOUBLES every $10$ years. After how many years does the town reach $10000$ people?
hint: Divide the target population by the starting population to see how much growth is needed.

hints.text: Divide the target population by the starting population to see how much growth is needed.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: going from $100$ to $400$ is $\times 4$, and $4 = 2^2$, so $2$ doublings. Same move — divide, then count doublings.
The growth needed is $10000 \div 1250 = 8$, and $8 = 2^3$, so you need $3$ doublings. Each doubling takes $10$ years.
Three doublings at $10$ years each take $3 \times 10 = 30$ years.

explanation: After $t$ years there have been $t/10$ doublings, so set up $1250 \cdot 2^{t/10} = 10000$.
Dividing both sides by $1250$ gives $2^{t/10} = 8 = 2^3$, so the exponents match and $t/10 = 3$.
Multiplying both sides by $10$ gives $t = 30$, so the town reaches $10000$ people after $30$ years.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count decade by decade
steps: The town hits $10{,}000$ people at year $30$.
